title: Signed shifts of an already normalized tensor comparison
statement: Fix a universe u, categories C,D with objects in Type (u+1) and morphisms in Type u, Grothendieck topologies J,K, ring sheaves R on J and S on K valued in CommRingCat (u+1), and a site functor F:C to D. Let o:Operation F R S be exact, and let a,b be the resolving tensor models of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data], with normalized shifts sa,sb. Given an ordinary tensor comparison mu satisfying its pure-unit equation and an already constructed TensorComparison t for o.leftModel, normalized on every resolving pair, both TensorComparisonShifts equations hold for the canonical exact-derived shift. Only the two shift squares are asserted: no ordinary, chain or derived comparison is constructed.

proof.text: Package the two shift squares as equalities of natural transformations on the product of derived categories. Use cochain tensor model rigidity with arbitrary target category Der S to test equality on flat-term K-flat pairs.

At each resolving pair use the supplied tensor shift normalization fields, the representative equation of t at the original and shifted pairs, and the exact-derived factors shift equation. Naturality moves the factor identifications past the comparison; cancel the representative isomorphisms and shifted images.

Test the remaining chain squares on every direct-sum tensor inclusion. The inverse ordinary comparison is natural by adjunction and the pure-unit formula. The first-variable square has coefficient one; the second-variable square has coefficient (-1)^(np) on both sides, preserved by additive pullback. The direct-sum universal property gives both chain equalities. Localize and use faithfulness to finish on all derived pairs. Zero shifts, empty sites and zero coefficient rings require no separate assumptions.

mathlib_searches.query: An exact derived pullback comparison for tensor products commutes with integer shifts when its tensor representatives and shift isomorphisms are normalized
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits. Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.DerivedCategory.ExactFunctor supplies the CommShift instance for mapDerivedCategory and NatTrans.CommShift for mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom. Other hits concern pullback of shifts and totalShift₂XIso. The factor compatibility is used in the argument; no hit proves both tensor comparison squares for arbitrary normalized resolving models.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use the canonical exact-derived factors shift instance, together with tensor normalization, chain shift calculations and faithful restriction; no match for the whole statement.

mathlib_searches.query: A natural tensor comparison between exact derived functors commutes with both shifts if it agrees with total tensor maps on K-flat representatives
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: Abelian.Ext.mapExactFunctor_hom, mapDerivedCategory CommShift, mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh and the Tor/Tor-prime functors and map lemmas. These cover exact-functor shifts or projective-resolution Tor, not the present comparison between arbitrary unbounded derived tensor models on ringed sites.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No complete match; retain the separate normalized-comparison shift result.

mathlib_searches.results: Twenty-five Mathlib source hits reported by msearch, including CategoryTheory/Shift/Localization.lean lines 239-241 and 306, Shift/CommShift.lean and Shift/CommShiftTwo.lean. Further direct source reading found the exact-derived factors CommShift instance in Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/ExactFunctor.lean at line 94 and the two total shift inclusion formulas in BifunctorShift.lean. These provide the component calculations, not the whole arbitrary-model comparison theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Use the existing normalization and shift APIs; prove the two total chain squares and descend their compatibility.
